previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, and obesity was admitted for acute decompensated heart failure following dietary indiscretion with high sodium intake and noncompliance with evening diuretic therapy. He presented with worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, significant lower extremity edema, and fluid overload. He was diuresed with IV furosemide, achieving nearly 15 liters of urine output. Due to persistent tachycardia and suboptimal rate control on metoprolol, he underwent transesophageal echocardiography which showed no intracardiac thrombus, followed by successful DC cardioversion to restore sinus rhythm. His INR was subtherapeutic on admission, and he remained on warfarin and adjusted metoprolol dosing. He improved clinically but left against medical advice before formal discharge instructions could be completed. He was advised on weight monitoring, sodium and fluid restriction, medication adherence, and follow-up with cardiology and primary care.
problems: Acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure

# Acute on chronic systolic and diastolic HF: EF ___. 
Exacerbation was most likely due to dietary indiscretion. Pt has 
h/o non-adherence but states he has been med compliant. His 
A-fib was not well rate controlled on admission, which may have 
contributed to his CHF exacerbation. Weight on admission was 342 
lbs which is exacly what he weighted at recent caridology appt 
on ___. When he was diagnosed with CHF in ___, his 
weight was 320 lbs. Nutrition consultant educated patient on 
dietary changes in CHF. Medication changes were made to optimize 
medical management of his CHF in conjunction with assistance 
from cardiology/heart failure consult. Pt was diuresed with 
lasix IV 40mg TID and transitioned to lasix 80mg PO BID once his 
creatinine slighlty increased. Metoprolol XL was increased to 
50mg daily. Ramipril was increased to 2.5mg daily but pt was 
slightly hypotensive with SBP ___ on day prior to his leaving. 
Plan was to decrease ramipril back to 1.25mg daily and increase 
metoprolol XL to 75mg daily for better rate control, but pt left 
AMA prior to evaluation on new medication regimen. Cardiology 
recommended intitiating spironolactone as outpatient after 
diuresis complete. Weight on discharge was 329 lbs, which may be 
his new dry weight as pt became pre-renal, but cardiology felt 
he could have been diuresed further. As pt did not stay for new 
prescriptions given medication changes, he was encouraged to 
follow up with his PCP for optimization of his medication 
regimen for his CHF. 
.  
# Atrial fibrillation: Pt has h/o a-flutter ablation. Pt in 
A-fib on admission with HR 94-115, which may have contributed to 
his CHF exacerbation. Pt monitored on telemetry with one 14 beat 
run of V-tach, which was asymptomatic. His metoprolol XL was 
increased to 50mg daily with HR 90-105. Plan was to increase to 
75mg daily for better rate control but pt left prior to 
initiating change. Pt was subtherapeutic on coumadin on 
admission with INR 1.3. His warfarin was increased to 7.5mg 
daily and INR at discharge was 2.3. However, no wafarin 
prescription and instructions could be given prior to pt 
leaving.  
.  
# Concern for Sleep Apnea - pt's body habitus puts him at high 
risk for OSA. He had events on continuous O2 sat monitoring in 
which his oxygen saturation decreased to 70-80% RA. Pt attempted 
to use CPAP on his first night in hospital, but was unable to 
tolerate it and refused CPAP on subseuqent nights. He did agree 
to outpatient polysomnography.
. 
# CAD equivalent: Pt had a clean cardiac catheterization in 
___, but does have a CAD equivalent in DM, meaning any MI might 
be silent, and this could have been a precipitant of 
decompensation of CHF. Cardiac enzymes negative (slightly 
elevated troponin may have been due to kidney function or demand 
ischemia). Pt continued on beta blocker, aspirin and statin.
